test_title: SSC Selection Post 2025 (Higher Secondary Level) Official Paper (Held On: 25 Jul, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
A sentence is provided in direct speech. From the four given options, choose the one that most accurately conveys the sentence in its corresponding indirect speech.

He said, "I have completed the project."

options.text: He said that he had completed the project.
He said that he has completed the project.
He said that he completed the project.
He said he completes the project.

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indirect Speech:** He said that he had completed the project.
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **"I have completed" becomes "he had completed"**
 
 
• The pronoun **"I"** changes to **"he"** to align with the subject of the reporting verb.
 
• The **Present Perfect** tense ("have completed") shifts to the **Past Perfect** tense ("had completed") because the reporting verb ("said") is in the past.
 
 
 
• **Conjunction:**
 
 
• The word **"that"** is used to introduce the reported clause, though it is often optional in spoken English.
 
 
 
• **Sentence Type:**
 
 
• This is an assertive sentence, so the structure remains a statement in indirect speech.
 
 
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"He said that he had completed the project."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2:** "He said that he has completed the project." 

 
 
• **Error:** This fails to apply the necessary backshift. "Has" must change to "had" when the reporting verb is in the past.
 
 
 
• **Option 3:** "He said that he completed the project." 
 
 
• **Error:** Changes the tense to Past Simple. While sometimes used in casual speech, the standard rule for Present Perfect in indirect speech is a shift to Past Perfect.
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** "He said he completes the project." 
 
 
• **Error:** Uses the Present Simple tense ("completes"), which incorrectly implies a habitual action or a current state, rather than a finished task.
